headline: Your ankle swelling improved after you stopped amlodipine, but your blood pressure was still above Dr. Smith’s goal, so Nurse Rivera planned a referral to Dr. Patel in cardiology.

followUps.title: Book your cardiology visit when the office calls
followUps.detail: Nurse Rivera said the referral to Dr. Patel would go in on October 28. Cardiology will call you to book. The usual wait is 4 to 6 weeks, roughly November 25 to December 9.

followUps.title: Bring your home blood pressure monitor
followUps.detail: Bring it the next time you see Nurse Rivera. Nurse Rivera will compare it with the clinic’s monitor.

instructions.text: Check your blood pressure at home before breakfast and again in the evening.
Before you check your blood pressure, sit for 5 minutes. Keep your feet flat and rest your arm on a table at heart level. Don’t have coffee in the 30 minutes before you check.

Call the clinic if the top number is over 160 more than twice in a week, if you have a bad headache with blurry vision, or if you have any chest pain. Nurse Rivera said “more than twice,” but you repeated it as “twice.”

unchanged.text: No medicine changes for now. You’re still off amlodipine. You take ramipril 10 mg and vitamin D in the morning, and atorvastatin 20 mg at night.

openQuestions.text: Is your home blood pressure monitor accurate?
openQuestions.resolvesWhen: When Nurse Rivera compares it with the clinic’s monitor.

openQuestions.text: What blood pressure plan will work best for you now that you’re off amlodipine?
openQuestions.resolvesWhen: When Dr. Patel reviews your blood pressure plan.

openQuestions.text: Will you need a heart scan?
openQuestions.resolvesWhen: Dr. Patel may decide to order one.
